name: slider
description: A range input with draggable thumbs. Supports single value, ranges (two thumbs), custom steps, and full keyboard control.

props.name: value
props.description: Controlled array of thumb values (number[]), e.g. [50] for single, [20, 80] for range

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: Default array of thumb values (number[]) for uncontrolled usage

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Callback on value change: (value: number[]) => void

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Accessible label for the slider as a whole. Mirrored onto a single thumb automatically; for range sliders prefer thumbLabels.

props.name: aria-labelledby
props.description: Id of an external visible label that names the slider.

props.name: thumbLabels
props.description: Per-thumb accessible labels (string[]). Required for range sliders so each thumb has a meaningful name (e.g. ['Minimum price', 'Maximum price']). For a single-thumb slider, the Root's aria-label is mirrored onto the thumb automatically and thumbLabels is only needed when overriding that default.

examples.title: Volume control with display
examples.description: Single-thumb slider paired with the live numeric value — the canonical 'continuous range with feedback' pattern

examples.title: Price-range filter
examples.description: Two-thumb range slider with per-thumb labels — the canonical e-commerce filter UI
examples.code:
<Slider
  defaultValue={[20, 80]}
  max={100}
  step={1}
  thumbLabels={["Minimum price", "Maximum price"]}
/>

ai.whenToUse: Use for continuous numeric inputs with a known range: volume, brightness, price range filter, opacity. Pair value with a visible number display when the exact value matters.
ai.whenNotToUse: Don't use when the user needs to enter an exact number (use Input type=number). Don't use for discrete choices (use Select or RadioGroup). Don't use for boolean on/off (use Switch).
commonMistakes: Using Slider for exact values without showing the number
Using step=1 for fractional values (set step=0.01)
Not providing aria-label / aria-labelledby when there's no visible label
Range slider with only Root aria-label and no thumbLabels — both thumbs fall back to '(N of 2)' indexed names instead of meaningful per-thumb labels
thumbLabels.length !== value.length — extra labels are ignored, missing labels fall back to indexed names (dev-mode warning)

antiPatterns.mistake: Using Slider with min=0/max=1 to represent on/off
antiPatterns.why: Slider is 'continuous range'. Switch is 'boolean'. Assistive tech announces them differently — Slider says '0 of 1, 1 of 1'; Switch says 'on / off'. Always reach for Switch when the values are binary.

antiPatterns.mistake: Using Slider for picking a number from a small discrete set (1–5 rating, 'pages per row')
antiPatterns.why: Sliders make exact target values hard to land on. RadioGroup gives 5 buttons that name themselves and are easier with assistive tech. Reach for Slider only when 50+ values are valid.

antiPatterns.mistake: Using Slider for the user to type a known exact number (price, age, count)
antiPatterns.why: Drag-to-set is slower and less accurate than typing. Use <Input type='number'> when the user has the exact value in mind.

ai.accessibilityNotes: Arrow keys step by step, Home/End jump to min/max, PageUp/PageDown step larger. Radix handles aria-valuemin/max/now. Each thumb has its own accessible name: explicit via thumbLabels[i], else mirrored from the Root's aria-label (single thumb) or indexed '(i of N)' fallback (range). Add aria-label / aria-labelledby on the Root when there's no visible label.
